Good web design Minneapolis customers trust starts with plain facts that are easy to find: the street you are on, the door to use, the hours you keep and the language you serve people in. A lot of the city's small businesses are owner-run shops, market stalls and family restaurants, many started by people who came to Minnesota from somewhere else. Their websites are often an old social page or a listing someone else wrote. That costs them customers who search, find nothing clear, and walk to the next shop.

Dominion Web Design Pro builds small business sites that fix that, one hand-written page at a time. Maurice Johnson writes every page himself, you see a free demo before any invoice, and the price is printed: $497, $997 or $1,997, one time.

Lake Street came back one storefront at a time

After the unrest of May 2020 hit businesses along Lake Street, the Lake Street Council started the We Love Lake Street fund. It raised more than $12 million from over 80,000 donors. With an independent oversight committee guiding it, the council had awarded about $7 million to roughly 350 businesses when Twin Cities Business profiled the effort, mostly for construction repairs and to replace lost inventory and equipment. A separate acquisition and predevelopment fund put $1.4 million in grants and forgivable loans toward 20 entrepreneurs who were rebuilding from the ground up.

Five years on, a council representative told KSTP that almost all of the businesses had come back, and that new businesses had filled the spaces of those that could not. That is a long road for any owner. It also left a quiet problem behind: a lot of online information about those businesses is out of date. A shop that reopened in a new spot, changed its hours or added catering may still show the old address on a stale listing. The website is the one place the owner controls, so it is where you say, in your own words, that you are open, where you are now and what has changed.

Markets where dozens of owners share one address

Some of the city's best known small businesses do not have their own building. Mercado Central, at Lake Street and Bloomington Avenue, grew out of organizing by Latino entrepreneurs that began in 1991. It opened as a cooperative of small vendors, most of them family-owned, and in 2019 the co-op bought the building it occupies. Its success helped launch the Latino Economic Development Center in 2003, which later helped develop the Midtown Global Market. Karmel Mall, a Somali shopping center, holds more than a hundred small businesses in suites, selling everything from clothing and food to insurance and accounting services.

A vendor inside a market has a search problem that a corner shop does not. Dozens of businesses share one street address, so a customer who finds the building still has to find you. Your site should give the suite or stall number, the entrance closest to you, where to park and what you sell, with photos of the counter itself.

Cedar-Riverside and customers who read more than one language

Somalis began arriving in Minneapolis in large numbers in the early 1990s, and by 1998 Cedar-Riverside had one of the largest Somali communities in Minnesota. Today about half of the neighborhood's roughly 8,000 residents are of East African descent, according to Augsburg University's neighborhood history.

Say who you serve

If your counter staff speak Somali, Oromo, Spanish or Amharic, put that on the home page and the contact page. It is one of the first things many customers want to know, and it costs nothing to say.

Be honest about translation

Maurice writes the pages in English, and translation is not part of the packages. If you want a second language on the site, tell us when you ask for the demo so the plan is clear from the start.

Keep the phone number tappable

Plenty of customers would rather call than fill in a form, especially for a food order or a tailoring job. A number that dials with one tap on a phone does more than a long form ever will.

Web design Minneapolis searchers use depends on the neighborhood

Google says local results depend mainly on relevance, distance and prominence: how well a listing matches the search, how far it is from the searcher or the place named, and how well known the business is. People in this city search by neighborhood and suburb as often as by city name, so the names on your pages matter.

Where you workWhat a customer might typeWhat your page should say
Northeast arts district"framing shop northeast minneapolis"Studio or shop hours, open studio days, whether visitors can drop in
Lake Street and the Midtown corridor"tailor lake street"Cross street, suite or stall number, parking, languages spoken
Uptown or the North Loop"salon north loop"Booking method, nearest landmark you can name honestly, price range
Edina, Bloomington, Eden Prairie"electrician eden prairie mn"Which suburbs you drive to and how soon you can usually come
St. Paul next door"caterer st paul"Whether you cross the river, and a page for St. Paul if you do

Northeast shows why the neighborhood name carries weight. Artists who had moved into old factory buildings held the first Art-A-Whirl open studio tour there in 1995. The Northeast Minneapolis Arts Association formed in 1997 and now has more than 1,600 members, and the arts district's boundaries were set in 2002 with help from the city. A frame shop or ceramics studio there gets searches for the district itself, and a page that names it plainly catches them.

A walk-through: one owner, one demo, one decision

Here is how it usually goes, using a made-up example rather than a real business. Say you run a small alterations shop in a market off Lake Street. You ask for the demo with your business name, the stall number and the languages you speak. Maurice builds a draft home page and a services page that lists hemming, wedding dress fittings and school uniform alterations in the words customers use, plus your hours and a map. You look at it on your phone. If it does not feel like your shop, you say no and owe nothing.

If you go ahead, Starter at $497 covers five pages and goes live in 7 to 14 days. A business that serves several neighborhoods or suburbs would look at Pro, $997, with ten pages plus ten city pages. Its AI chat widget is free for 14 days, then $297 a month. Agency, $1,997, starts with keyword research across your whole area and builds a page for each town and service worth having, delivered in waves, the first live inside two weeks. It includes setup of an AI phone agent, which is free for 7 days and then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time, separate from the one-time price. We do not sell page counts: a few honest pages beat a stack of thin ones.

Custom web design here means the words and layout are made for your business, not dropped into a theme. Professional means the basics work every time: the phone number dials, the form reaches your inbox, the hours are right.

Free help for Minneapolis owners before you spend a dollar

  • City of Minneapolis Small Business Team. Its Business Technical Assistance Program offers up to 50 hours of no-cost consulting on things like business plans, licensing and operations, through a network of more than 25 service providers. The city's list shows each provider's target community and languages.
  • Lake Street Council. The group behind the We Love Lake Street fund and its grants and forgivable loans for rebuilding owners.
  • MCCD Open to Business. A program of the Metropolitan Consortium of Community Developers serving Minneapolis, Saint Paul and suburban communities across the seven-county metro.
  • Small Business Development Centers. Minnesota has nine SBDCs, plus satellite centers, run with the state's Department of Employment and Economic Development. Neighboring Richfield points its owners to the center at the University of St. Thomas for free consulting.

Common questions

How do I pick a Minneapolis web designer for a small shop?

Whether you hire one designer or a web design company in Minneapolis, ask three things before you sign. Who writes the words on each page? What is the full first-year cost, including hosting? Who owns the site if you leave? Then look at something built for your business, not a portfolio of other people's sites. Maurice Johnson writes and builds each of our sites himself, the prices are printed, you own the finished site, and you see a free demo before you pay anything. He works remotely from East Texas, so there is no in-person meeting in Minneapolis.

What does web design in Minneapolis cost for a small business?

Quotes in any big city run from a few hundred dollars to many thousands, depending on how much is custom and who does the work. Ours are one-time prices: Starter is $497 for five pages, Pro is $997 for ten pages plus ten city pages, and Agency is $1,997 for keyword research and a page for each town and service worth targeting. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

Is responsive web design included, so the site works on phones?

Yes, on every package. Responsive simply means the same site rearranges itself to fit a phone, a tablet or a desktop screen. Most people looking up a shop's hours or address are doing it on a phone, often while standing on the sidewalk, so we check every page at phone width before it goes live.

Do you build ecommerce or WordPress sites in Minneapolis?

Online stores are not part of our packages, and we will say so up front rather than sell you something half finished. If you need a full store with a cart and inventory, a store platform or an ecommerce specialist is the better fit. On platforms: each site is hand-built and you own it. If you need WordPress or another specific platform, say so when you ask for the demo and you will get a straight answer before you spend anything.

Can the site also cover Eden Prairie, Edina or St. Paul?

Yes, if you really serve those places. A plumber or caterer who works across the metro should have a page for each area that matters, written about that place. The Pro package includes ten city pages, so web design for Eden Prairie MN customers, St. Paul customers and Bloomington customers can each get its own page instead of one long list of suburb names.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
